# Error-Handling Checklist: Implementation-Notes Capture (ART-012)

**Purpose**: Validate that the error-handling requirements around the
implementation-notes record are complete, unambiguous, consistent, and
measurable before implementation
**Created**: 2026-08-10
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

Depth: standard. Audience: reviewer at PR time. Focus areas, taken from the
requesting prompt: fail-open completeness, the gap destination and SC-004's
checkability against it, missing versus unparseable reporting fields, the
failure mode of the fail-open path itself, and failure isolation inside a
parallel-run collection batch.

Run 1 found six missing requirements. All six were remediated in `spec.md` and
`plan.md`, mirrored into `contracts/implementation-notes-record.md`, and
re-verified in run 2. The Resolutions section at the foot records what closed
each one.

## Fail-Open Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are requirements defined stating that a failure to create the record leaves the task outcome unchanged? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004, §US1 AS-6]
- [x] CHK002 Are requirements defined stating that a failure to append an entry leaves the phase outcome unchanged? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004, §SC-004]
- [x] CHK003 Are the failure causes the fail-open path must absorb enumerated rather than left to the reader? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK004 Is fail-open stated as a binding requirement rather than only as design rationale? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, Plan §Failure behavior]
- [x] CHK005 Are requirements defined for whether a failed write is retried before the gap is recorded, so an implementer cannot add a blocking retry loop and still claim conformance? [Resolved R1, Spec §FR-004, Plan §Failure behavior]
- [x] CHK006 Is the record's exhaust status stated, so a reader can tell that no downstream step is entitled to block on it? [Clarity, Spec §Key Entities, Plan §Failure behavior]

## Gap Destination and SC-004 Measurability

- [x] CHK007 Is the destination of the recorded gap named specifically enough that a verifier knows the one place to look? [Clarity, Plan §Failure behavior, Contracts §Fail-open]
- [x] CHK008 Is the gap destination unambiguously distinct from the implementation-notes record itself, so the failure is never written to the file that just failed? [Resolved R2, Spec §FR-004, Contracts §Fail-open]
- [x] CHK009 Are requirements defined for what the recorded gap must identify — which attempt, and which operation failed — so SC-004's "readable afterwards" can be objectively checked? [Resolved R3, Spec §FR-004, §SC-004]
- [x] CHK010 Can SC-004 be objectively verified against the named destination without reading the implementation? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004, Plan §Failure behavior]
- [x] CHK011 Are the spec's abstract phrasing and the plan's concrete destination consistent rather than competing? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, Plan §Failure behavior]

## Missing or Unparseable Reporting Field

- [x] CHK012 Are requirements defined for an executor that omits the reporting field entirely? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-003]
- [x] CHK013 Is the recorded value for an omitted field specified as the same literal as an explicit report of nothing? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, §SC-003, Contracts §Coverage]
- [x] CHK014 Are requirements defined for a summary whose reporting field is present but cannot be extracted — malformed block, truncated output, heading collision — and is that case classified as a nothing-reported entry or as an FR-004 gap? [Resolved R4, Spec §FR-003, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK015 Are requirements consistent between FR-003's "returns no reporting field at all" clause and the contract's coverage row for a route that emits no task-result block? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, Contracts §Coverage]
- [x] CHK016 Is the boundary between a reporting-content problem and a record-write failure drawn so the two never claim the same case? [Resolved R4, Spec §FR-003, Contracts §Fail-open]

## Failure of the Fail-Open Path Itself

- [x] CHK017 Are requirements defined for the case where recording the gap also fails, or where the gap destination is the unwritable path? [Resolved R5, Spec §FR-004, §SC-004, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK018 Is the failure path bounded to a stated number of fallback levels, so it cannot recurse or loop? [Resolved R5, Spec §FR-004, Contracts §Fail-open]
- [x] CHK019 Is there a stated invariant that no failure anywhere in this feature's write path can change a task or phase outcome? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, §SC-004]

## Failure Isolation in a Parallel-Run Collection Batch

- [x] CHK020 Are requirements defined stating whether a failed append for one task in a collected parallel run stops or spares the remaining tasks' entries in that same batch? [Resolved R6, Spec §FR-004, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK021 Are requirements defined for whether a batch that partially failed still permits the next run to be dispatched? [Resolved R6, Spec §FR-004, Plan §Orchestrator append contract]
- [x] CHK022 Is SC-001's per-attempt entry count reconciled with the fail-open path, so a run with a failed append is not read as a requirement violation? [Resolved R7, Spec §SC-001, §FR-004]

## Record Lifecycle Failure Coverage

- [x] CHK023 Do the requirements state whether the orchestrator creates a missing containing directory or treats the missing directory as a write failure? [Resolved R8, Spec §FR-002, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK024 Are the resume-path failure requirements defined, so a failed lifecycle step never truncates an existing record or writes a second header? [Coverage, Spec §FR-002, Contracts §Lifecycle]
- [x] CHK025 Are requirements defined for a partially written entry, so additive-only in SC-005 stays satisfiable after a failed write? [Assumption, Spec §FR-003, §SC-005]
- [x] CHK026 Is the fail-open assumption's status recorded honestly, given the sibling precedent is recorded intent rather than shipped code? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]

## Cross-Artifact Consistency

- [x] CHK027 Do spec, plan, and the record contract state the same failure behavior without one being stricter than another? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, Plan §Failure behavior, Contracts §Fail-open]
- [x] CHK028 Is the platform-parity claim extended to failure behavior, not only to the successful record format? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, Contracts §Platform parity]

## Resolutions

- **R1 — retry semantics (CHK005).** FR-004 now states a failed write MUST NOT
  be retried. `plan.md` §Failure behavior gives the reason: a retry ladder on a
  file the phase does not depend on is the one way this path could stall the
  phase it exists to protect.
- **R2 — destination is not the failed file (CHK008).** FR-004 now says the gap
  goes to the record of the run, "never the implementation-notes record that
  just failed", closing a circular reading of the original wording.
- **R3 — gap content (CHK009).** FR-004 and SC-004 now require the gap to name
  the attempt or lifecycle step and the operation that failed. SC-004 was
  otherwise checkable only as "some gap exists somewhere".
- **R4 — unreadable reporting field (CHK014, CHK016).** FR-003 now covers a
  field that cannot be read out of the returned summary alongside a field that
  is absent. Both record that nothing was reported, and FR-003 states plainly
  that neither is a write failure, so neither takes FR-004's gap path.
- **R5 — the fail-open path's own failure (CHK017, CHK018).** FR-004 now bounds
  the failure path to exactly one fallback level. If the gap destination is
  itself the unwritable path, the second failure is surfaced in the run's own
  output and the run carries on, with no retry, no third destination, and no
  escalation. SC-004 makes that measurable.
- **R6 — blast radius (CHK020, CHK021).** FR-004 now states entries are written
  independently: a failure recorded for one attempt stops neither the remaining
  entries in the same collection batch nor the next dispatch.
- **R7 — SC-001 under fail-open (CHK022).** SC-001 now excludes an attempt whose
  append failed and was recorded as a gap, with the gap standing in the entry's
  place, so a fail-open run does not read as a violation.
- **R8 — missing containing directory (CHK023).** FR-002 now folds creating the
  containing directory into creating the record, so an absent directory is a
  thing to create rather than a failure to report. This aligns the requirement
  with Design Concept Q8, which claims the create step guarantees the file and
  its process directory exist.

- Check items off as completed: `[x]`

  defect in an implementation. Every one is closed above.
